newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds higher after Jewish holiday.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds higher after Jewish holiday.

text.p: Israeli bonds ended higher on Thursday as demand for short-term CPI-linked bonds revived in response to higher yields, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.11 pct to 106.37
Volume including Makams was 150 million shekels.
"Today traders rediscovered short-term CPI-linked bonds after ignoring them in favour of the long-term bonds. Yields on these bonds are a high six percent," said Tiki Hadad of IBI Investment House.
She said prices for CPI-linked long bonds also rose but at a slower rate. Demand for the bonds has been rising in expectation of a tightening supply and of a cut in interest rates, Hadad said.
"The market is feeling the shortage in bonds and is expecting interest rates to go down," she said.
The Bank of Israel is scheduled to announce its July monetary programme, including interest rates, on June 23. The base rate has been unchanged at 13.9 percent since the end of February.

Three months of budget surpluses and increased privatisation revenues, which have reduced the government's need to raise debt, are causing some traders to brace themselves for a tight supply of bonds.

Hadad said prices for unlinked bonds rose on Thursday in response to the absence of any new issues this week and the outlook for low inflation. The market is now looking for inflation of less than nine percent over the next 12 months.
She added that unlinked-bond prices reflected a catching-up after two days of lost trading. Markets were closed on Tuesday and Wednesday because of the Jewish holiday of Shavuot.
Yields on Makams are between 13.5 percent and 13.8 percent and between 13.33 percent and 14.21 percent on the unlinked bonds, a trader at Jerusalem Capital Markets said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
